ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It exhibits highly variable dorsal patterns ranging from mottled brown to green, often featuring a distinct dark interorbital bar and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes akroparallagi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, triangular or V-shaped marking between its eyes, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Variable Bush Frog inhabits evergreen forests and tea plantations in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Variable Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of high-altitude shrubbery.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes akroparallagi* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes akroparallagi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Variable Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests and grasslands.
